title: All-Hands run-of-show + staff asks (Q4 proposal)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight run-of-show and staff-asks bundle for the proposed Q4 all-hands (target week of Oct 5). It is a planning artifact: run-of-show, speaker assignments, slide/backstage needs, and explicit 'asks' we will surface to the org. The goal is to give executives and leads a single page they can react to quickly and for ops to run from during dry runs and rehearsal.

Audience:
- Exec leadership (CEO, CTO, Head of Product, Head of Ops)
- People leads and functional leads (eng, infra, product, GtM)
- Company at large (all-hands attendees)

Key outcomes we want from this all-hands:
1) Communicate top-level Q4 company priority and reasons for shifts in focus (short, crisp narrative).
2) Surface revised company-level OKRs (draft) and explain measurement approach and owner cadence.
3) Share product roadmap highlights tied to customer impact + performance targets (latency/price/capacity wins).
4) Make 3 clear staff asks (concrete actions teams should take in next 30–60 days).
5) Celebrate wins and spotlight two customer stories.

High-level narrative arc (3 mins per slide pacing, ~45 minute session + 15 min AMA):
- Intro / framing (CEO) — 5 minutes
  - Current state quick recap (where we are vs. Q3 commitments)
  - Why Q4 matters (revenue cadence, Dedicated/RPO launches, compliance expansions)
- Company OKRs overview (Head of Product / Head of GTM) — 8 minutes
  - Present 3 company-level OKRs with 1–2 supporting metrics each
  - Call out owners and how teams should interpret them
- Product & roadmap highlights (VP Product) — 10 minutes
  - Demo clip or short recorded demo (30–60s) for a top feature
  - Performance metrics: p50/p95 latency improvements, cost per 1K tokens reductions, Dedicated capacity milestones
- Reliability & Private deliveries (Head of Eng / SRE) — 6 minutes
  - Status of Private deployments, compliance packages, and SLOs
  - What to do during capacity-constrained windows (operational playbook link)
- Customer spotlight (Solutions Eng + Customer Success) — 6 minutes
  - Two short mini-case studies (1 slide each): startup use and mid-market enterprise
- People & hiring update (Head of People) — 3 minutes
  - Org health highlights, hiring priorities, upcoming interview blitz
- Staff asks / what we need from the company (CEO) — 4 minutes
  - Three concrete asks (below)
- Closing + logistics for follow-ups + AMA intro (CEO) — 3 minutes
- Live AMA (panel: CEO, Head of Product, Head of Eng, Head of GTM) — 15 minutes

Proposed company-level OKR drafts (short form):
- OKR 1: Make inference predictable and 3x more cost-efficient for targeted enterprise workloads
  - KR1: Reduce average cost per 1K real-customer tokens by 30% across top 10 customers
  - KR2: Achieve p95 generation latency <= 600ms for hosted small-model tier
  - Owners: VP Product, Head of Serving Runtime

- OKR 2: Expand Dedicated and Private adoption with enterprise-ready controls
  - KR1: 25% increase in Dedicated committed capacity bookings q/q
  - KR2: 3 signed Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with enterprise contracts
  - Owners: Head of Sales, Head of Private Deployments

- OKR 3: Make operations measurable and self-serve for platform teams
  - KR1: 90% of recurring customers onboard to per-route observability within 60 days
  - KR2: Reduce mean time to detect production regressions by 40% via auto-evals and alerting
  - Owners: Head of Console, Head of Observability

Notes on wording: these are deliberately metric-focused; we'll present as drafts with a 1-week feedback window following the all-hands and then iterate.

Staff asks (the 'asks' need to be explicit and actionable):
1) Quality guardrails: engineering teams run the top 10 customer prompt suites through the new eval harness and tag regressions by Mar 1 (owner: Applied ML / Solutions Eng).
2) Product telemetry adoption: all feature rollout owners add the observability recipe (route-level dashboards + tracing) to launch checklist for every customer-facing route (owner: Product Leads)
3) Hiring support: Heads of Eng should identify 3 internal hiring referral pushes (IC-focused) and be ready to run a week-long interview blitz in early Q4 (owner: People Ops + Eng managers)

Logistics / runbook items (operational details):
- Date/time: proposed Oct 7, 10:00–11:00 PT (block for whole company 9–11 PT for rehearsals/backstage).
- Format: Zoom webinar with internal attendee-only AMA via Slido; recorded and posted to Confluence + short highlights clip for async teams in APAC.
- Slides: limit to 15 slides. Each speaker gets 1–3 slides. Keep slides visual with 1 headline per slide.
- Demo: short recorded clip (30–60s) + 1 live demo fallback. Host: Solutions Eng; fallback speaker: VP Product. Pre-record by Sep 20.
- Rehearsal schedule: Dry run 1 (exec only) Sep 24; Full run (with all speakers + ops) Sep 30; Dress rehearsal Oct 6 morning.
- Backstage ops: Ops Slack channel #allhands-backstage, production lead (Leena), AV lead (Jordan), recording & cut highlights (Sofia).
- Accessibility: captions on for live, slide deck uploaded with alt text for images, and recorded clip transcript.

Speaker checklist (one-pagers to be created for each):
- 1-line headline for slide + 2 supporting bullets
- 1–2 data points (source + last updated date)
- If asking for action from teams, include exact owner and timeline
- Slide deck filename convention: AH-Q4-2026-Speaker-lastname-v1.pptx

Communications & pre-read cadence:
- Save the date email (ops) — Aug 20
- Speaker prep packets (ops -> speakers) — Sep 10
- Company pre-read + OKR one-pager (short PDF) — distributed Sep 28
- Reminder + link to AMA tool — Oct 6

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: OKRs perceived as too top-down / not actionable at team level. Mitigation: attach team-level interpretation templates and host post-all-hands office hours with product and ops.
- Risk: Demo flake / live demo fails. Mitigation: pre-record primary demo and keep a short recorded fallback clip; longer live demo gated to backstage signoff.
- Risk: Timing overruns. Mitigation: strict timekeeper (ops) with visible countdown; trim AMA by dropping panelists if needed.

Follow-up plan (post-all-hands):
- Publish slides + recording within 24 hours (ops)
- Feedback window open for 7 days (Confluence comments + Slack thread)
- Finalize OKRs after feedback window and publish definitive owner list and measurement dashboard (product ops)
- Run office hours: week after all-hands for teams to ask about translating company OKRs into team OKRs

Open questions (for execs to resolve before finalizing slides):
- Do execs want to reduce OKRs to two instead of three to simplify messaging? (pros/cons table attached in linked confluence doc).
- Which customer stories can be cleared for public mention? (legal checks with CS required)
- Do we have a final measurement baseline for cost per 1K tokens that leadership is comfortable publishing?

Appendix (short admin items):
- Slide permissions: please share final deck to ops folder by Oct 2 EOD (ops will produce deck master)
- Recording owner: Sofia (for cut highlights)
- Reporter for all-hands notes / actions: Samir (publish action tracker)

Next steps (this doc lifecycle):
- Share this draft with execs for 48-hour review (Leena)
- Agree date and lock speakers (CEO + Head of Product) by Mar 20
- Ops to create speaker one-pagers and folder structure in Drive (ops)

Notes to reviewers: this is a working doc. Please comment inline or drop feedback in #all-hands-planning. If you are a speaker, add your slide headline in the sheet linked above and mark any resource needs (demo, metrics, recording) by Mar 25.
